title: TESU BA in Biology: Course Map
body:
Thomas Edison State University, Bachelor of Arts in Biology, current catalog. 120 credits: 45 general education, 60 area of study, 15 free electives. Confirm the catalog-year plan with a TESU advisor before registering; this map is a study guide, not the registrar.

## Area of study: required (45 credits)

| TESU course | Credits | Where it is at TESU | Rounds module | PA prerequisite? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| General Biology I with lab | 4 | Transfer required | Biology I | Yes (most programs) |
| General Biology II with lab | 4 | Transfer required | Biology II | Yes (most programs) |
| Cell Biology | 3 | Transfer required | Cell Biology | Sometimes |
| Genetics | 3 | Transfer required | Genetics | Sometimes |
| CHE-1210 General Chemistry I with lab | 4 | TESU | Chemistry I | Yes |
| CHE-1220 General Chemistry II with lab | 4 | TESU | Chemistry II | Yes |
| Organic Chemistry I with lab | 4 | Transfer required | Organic Chemistry | Yes (or biochemistry) |
| Organic Chemistry II with lab | 4 | Transfer required | Organic Chemistry (second half) | Sometimes |
| BIO-2510 Introduction to Microbiology with lab | 4 | TESU | Microbiology | Yes |
| PHY-1150 Physics I with lab | 4 | TESU | Physics for the Health Sciences | Sometimes |
| PHY-1160 Physics II with lab | 4 | TESU | Physics for the Health Sciences (second half) | Sometimes |
| MAT-1290 Precalculus | 3 | TESU | Precalculus | No (statistics is the usual math prerequisite) |

## Area of study: biology electives (12 credits) and capstone (3)

| Course | Credits | Rounds module | Why take it |
|---|---|---|---|
| BIO-2110 Anatomy and Physiology I with lab | 4 | A&P I | Required by nearly every PA program |
| BIO-2120 Anatomy and Physiology II with lab | 4 | A&P II | Required by nearly every PA program |
| Biochemistry (transfer, if chosen as an elective) | 3–4 | Biochemistry | Accepted in place of organic chemistry II by many programs |
| Upper-level biology (3000+) to reach the 18-credit upper-level rule | varies | Pre-PA track | Programs like to see rigor beyond the minimum |
| LIB-4970 Liberal Arts Capstone, Natural Sciences | 3 | none | Required to graduate |

## General education science (6 credits)

| Course | Credits | Rounds module |
|---|---|---|
| EAS-1010 General Earth Science | 3 | none (not a PA prerequisite) |
| BIO-2080 The Science of Nutrition | 3 | Nutrition |

## General education, the rest (39 credits)

| Block | Courses | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Intellectual and practical skills (15) | ENC-1010, ENC-1020 writing; COM-2090 public speaking; MAT-1210 college algebra; SOS-1100 information literacy | Prior credits transfer here first |
| Civic and global leadership (9) | SOC-1010 sociology; ETH-2200 ethical leadership; POS-1100 American government | |
| Knowledge of human cultures (15) | SOC-2100; HIS-1130; FIL-1100; two of SOC-2910, HIS-1140, HIS-1210, HUM-1030, PHI-1300 | |

## PA prerequisites the degree does not include by default

| Prerequisite | How to cover it | Rounds module |
|---|---|---|
| Statistics | Use a free elective or transfer it | Statistics |
| General and abnormal psychology | Free electives or transfer | Psychology |
| Medical terminology | Many programs accept a course or waive it | Medical Terminology (Foundations) |
| Biochemistry | Elective or transfer | Biochemistry |

## Rules that shape the plan

- Six major courses are **transfer required** (General Biology I and II, Cell Biology, Genetics, Organic Chemistry I and II): take them at a community college or another accredited school and transfer them in. Confirm each course's transferability with TESU first.
- At least **18 credits in the major must be 3000 level or above**.
- At least **30 credits must be completed through TESU** (residency minimum since 2021).
- Calculus is recommended, not required.
- Labs matter for PA programs: choose lab sections wherever a course offers one.

## Suggested order while working as an ED tech

1. Transfer evaluation, then the general education blocks your prior credits do not already cover.
2. General Biology I and II with lab (transfer), alongside the Biology I and II modules.
3. General Chemistry I and II with lab at TESU, alongside Chemistry I and II.
4. A&P I and II with lab at TESU, alongside A&P I and II and the Pre-PA anatomy modules.
5. Microbiology at TESU; Genetics and Cell Biology by transfer.
6. Organic Chemistry I and II with lab (transfer) or Organic I plus Biochemistry.
7. Physics I and II, Precalculus, Statistics, Psychology, Nutrition.
8. Upper-level biology electives to reach 18 credits, then the capstone.
